Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

society noun

people living together; the community at large

also human society, modern society, in society, society at large

classical

Cic. Off. 1.53: gradūs autem plūrēs sunt societātis hominum
Cic. Amic. 20: societās generis hūmānī (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. society: societās hūmāna

societās, societātis f.

noun, third declension

society: the fellowship of people living together

Lewis & Short: fellowship, community, society, implying union for a common purpose. Cicero speaks of societās hominum or generis hūmānī, human society, in widening circles from the family (Off. 1.53–54).

Other words

  • cīvitās, cīvitātis f. — society as an organized community of citizens

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.53: interius etiam est ejusdem esse cīvitātis

    The society one belongs to as a citizen (see state, a country).

  • convīctus, convīctūs m. — life together, social life

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. society: hominum convīctus

    See social.

Examples

  • Gradūs autem plūrēs sunt societātis hominum.

    Human society has several degrees.Cic. Off. 1.53

  • prīma societās in ipsō conjugiō est, proxima in līberīs, deinde ūna domus, commūnia omnia

    the first society is marriage itself, the next is children, then one household with everything sharedCic. Off. 1.54

See also social, community, people, state, society.

SourcesLewis & Short: societas · Lewis & Short: civitas · Lewis & Short: convictus
